questions.q: Retinal detachment is the separation of the neurosensory retina from the ___ with collection of subretinal fluid.
questions.exp: RD: separation of neurosensory retina from retinal pigment epithelium and collection of subretinal fluid. (Book p169)

questions.q: Which investigation is the investigation of choice (IOC) for retinal detachment in the book?
questions.exp: Investigations: Indirect ophthalmoscopy: IOC; also OCT and B-scan ultrasonography. (Book p169)

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed among the investigations for retinal detachment?
questions.exp: Listed investigations: indirect ophthalmoscopy (IOC), OCT and B-scan ultrasonography. (Book p169)

questions.q: In the 'Normal' diagram beside the investigations, the labelled layers from top to bottom are:
questions.exp: Normal: NSR / Subretinal space / RPE. In the retinal detachment diagram the space is filled with Fluid between NSR and RPE. (Book p169)

questions.q: How does the book classify retinal detachment?
opts: Primary RD (tractional), and Secondary RD (rhegmatogenous and exudative)
Primary/Rhegmatogenous RD, and Secondary RD (tractional and exudative)
Rhegmatogenous RD, tractional RD, and Secondary RD (exudative only)
questions.exp: Types: RD -> Primary/Rhegmatogenous RD; Secondary RD -> Tractional and Exudative. (Book p169)

questions.q: The pathogenesis of rhegmatogenous RD begins with ___ (liquefaction of vitreous), followed by posterior vitreous detachment.
opts: Entry of fluid into the subretinal space
questions.exp: Pathogenesis: Syneresis (liquefaction of vitreous) -> posterior vitreous detachment (PVD). (Book p169)

questions.q: Which sequence follows posterior vitreous detachment in the pathogenesis of RRD?
opts: Dynamic vitreoretinal traction from attached vitreous, retinal breaks develop, fluid enters subretinal space
Retinal breaks develop, dynamic vitreoretinal traction, fluid enters subretinal space
Fluid enters subretinal space, retinal breaks develop, dynamic vitreoretinal traction
Dynamic vitreoretinal traction, fluid enters subretinal space, retinal breaks develop
questions.exp: PVD -> dynamic vitreoretinal traction from attached parts of vitreous -> retinal breaks develop -> fluid enters subretinal space. (Book p169)

questions.q: The pathogenesis figure with arrows on the curved retina is labelled with:
opts: Retina, posterior vitreous face, subretinal fluid and vitreoretinal traction
Retina, detached parts of retina, attached parts of retina and retinal break
Retina, detached parts of retina, attached parts of retina and vitreoretinal traction
Neurosensory retina, RPE, attached parts of retina and vitreoretinal traction
questions.exp: Figure labels: Retina, Detached parts of retina, Attached parts of retina, Vitreoretinal traction. (Book p169)

questions.q: What is the most common cause of rhegmatogenous retinal detachment?
questions.exp: Causes: Pathological myopia (m/c), blunt trauma, cataract surgery (aphakia), lattice degeneration of retina. (Book p169)

questions.q: All of the following are listed causes of primary/rhegmatogenous RD EXCEPT:
questions.exp: RRD causes: pathological myopia, blunt trauma, cataract surgery (aphakia), lattice degeneration. Diabetic retinopathy is the m/c cause of tractional RD (p171). (Book p169)

questions.q: The book explains the 'flashes of light' of RRD (written as photophobia) by stretching of ___, which sends ectopic neural impulses to the brain.
questions.exp: Photophobia: Flashes of light (Stretching of nerve fibers -> Ectopic neural impulses to brain). (Book p169)

questions.q: In RRD, small black flying dots (floaters) are due to:
questions.exp: Floaters: Small black flying dots (d/t vitreal opacities). (Book p169)

questions.q: A patient reports floaters and flashes, then a curtain falling in front of the eye with sudden, painless loss of vision. Which diagnosis fits the book's symptom list?
questions.exp: RRD symptoms: flashes of light, floaters, curtain falling in front of eye, loss of vision sudden & painless. (Book p169)

questions.q: How is the detached retina described in RRD?
opts: Pale and flat with cherry red spot
questions.exp: Signs: Detached retina: Gray/opaque, convex shaped. (Concave shape belongs to tractional RD, p171.) (Book p170)

questions.q: In RRD the extent of the detachment goes up to the ___.
questions.exp: Signs: Extent of RD till ora serrata. (Book p170)

questions.q: Slit-lamp examination of the anterior vitreous shows a tobacco-dust appearance in a patient with RD. Which sign is this?
questions.exp: Signs 3: Shafer's sign - tobacco-dust appearance. (Book p170)

questions.q: Shafer's sign is due to deposition of brown pigmented cells at the ___ surface of the vitreous.
questions.exp: Shafer's sign: d/t deposition of brown pigmented cells at the anterior surface of vitreous. (Book p170)

questions.q: The eye diagram drawn beside the signs list is labelled with:
questions.exp: The eye diagram's labels: RD and Shafer's sign. (Book p170)

questions.q: Under the photograph captioned 'U shaped retinal tear', the book gives which m/c location?
questions.exp: U shaped retinal tear - m/c location: Superotemporal quadrant. (The photograph before it is captioned RD.) (Book p170)

questions.q: An OCT scan captioned 'Longstanding RRD' is annotated with which features?
opts: RD, subretinal fluid and Shafer's sign
RD, high water marks and intraretinal cysts
Retinal breaks, subretinal fluid and RPE
RD, subretinal fluid and intraretinal cysts
questions.exp: OCT of longstanding RRD labels: RD, Subretinal fluid, Intraretinal cysts. (Book p170)

questions.q: What are Lincoff rules used for?
opts: To decide the duration of silicone oil tamponade
To locate breaks in the retina
questions.exp: Lincoff rules: Rules to locate breaks in retina (repeated in the note at the end of the page). (Book p170)

questions.q: Sign 4 of RRD in the book is ___ (relative afferent pupillary defect).
questions.exp: Signs 4: RAPD (Relative afferent pupillary defect). (Book p170)

questions.q: In chronic RD, subretinal demarcation lines known as 'high water marks' (and retinal atrophy) appear after more than ___.
questions.exp: In chronic RD: retinal atrophy; subretinal demarcation lines K/a high water marks (> 3 months). (Book p170)

questions.q: Intraretinal cysts appear in chronic RD after more than:
questions.exp: Intraretinal cysts (> 1 year). (Book p170)

questions.q: What prophylaxis does the book give for retinal breaks?
opts: Laser photocoagulation to seal the breaks (usually superotemporal quadrant)
Pneumatic retinopexy with SF6 in the inferior quadrant
questions.exp: Prophylaxis: Laser photocoagulation to seal breaks (usually superotemporal quadrant). (Book p170)

questions.q: In the treatment flowchart, a mobile retina is managed by:
questions.exp: Treatment: mobile retina -> Tamponade -> Internal / External. Immobile retina -> vitrectomy + subretinal fluid drainage. (Book p170)

questions.q: Pneumatic retinopexy uses ___ gas.
questions.exp: Internal tamponade 1. Pneumatic retinopexy: uses SF6 or C3F8 (Propane). (Book p170)

questions.q: Pneumatic retinopexy is done for breaks in which location?
opts: Breaks at the ora serrata only
questions.exp: Pneumatic retinopexy: Done in superior breaks. (Book p170)

questions.q: Silicone oil tamponade is injected into the ___ and removed after ___.
questions.exp: Silicone oil: injected into vitreous cavity; removed after 8-12 weeks. (Book p170)

questions.q: After silicone oil tamponade, oil leaks into the anterior chamber and collects superiorly, forming an inverse hypopyon. What is this complication called?
questions.exp: Silicone oil complication: Hyperoleon -> oil leaks into anterior chamber and collects superiorly (inverse hypopyon). (Book p170)

questions.q: In scleral buckling, the scleral weight pushes the ___ anteriorly.
questions.exp: External tamponade: Scleral buckling (Scleral weight pushes RPE anteriorly). (Book p170)

questions.q: An RD has an immobile retina due to proliferative vitreo-retinopathy, which causes membrane formation and scarring. Which treatment does the flowchart give?
questions.exp: Immobile retina: in proliferative vitreo-retinopathy (causes membrane formation & scarring) -> Vitrectomy + subretinal fluid drainage. (Book p170)

questions.q: Match the secondary RD with its pathology — 1) Tractional RD  2) Exudative RD  … A) Exudation into subretinal space  B) Static vitreoretinal traction  C) Dynamic vitreoretinal traction
questions.exp: Pathology: tractional RD - static vitreoretinal traction; exudative RD - exudation into subretinal space. (RRD has dynamic traction, p169.) (Book p171)

questions.q: What is the most common cause of tractional retinal detachment?
questions.exp: Tractional RD etiology: Diabetic retinopathy (m/c), ROP, penetrating trauma, sickle cell retinopathy. (Book p171)

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as an etiology of tractional RD?
questions.exp: Tractional RD: DR (m/c), ROP, penetrating trauma, sickle cell retinopathy. VKH syndrome is listed under exudative RD. (Book p171)

questions.q: A tractional RD cause shows Roth spots, described as hemorrhage with clear centre. Which cause is this?
questions.exp: Sickle cell retinopathy (Roth spots (+): Hemorrhage with clear centre). (Book p171)

questions.q: What is the most common cause of exudative RD?
questions.exp: Exudative RD etiology: Choroidal melanoma (m/c). (Book p171)

questions.q: A woman with toxemia of pregnancy develops a retinal detachment. Which type of secondary RD does the book list it under?
opts: Chronic RD with high water marks
questions.exp: Exudative RD etiology: choroidal melanoma (m/c), toxemia of pregnancy, Coat's disease, VKH syndrome, central serous retinopathy. (Book p171)

questions.q: Which is NOT listed as an etiology of exudative RD?
questions.exp: Exudative RD: choroidal melanoma, toxemia of pregnancy, Coat's disease, VKH syndrome, central serous retinopathy. ROP is a tractional RD cause. (Book p171)

questions.q: A patient has gradual, painless loss of vision and the detachment is concave in shape. Which secondary RD is this?
questions.exp: Tractional RD clinical features: loss of vision gradual & painless; shape of RD concave. (Book p171)

questions.q: True or false — 'Tractional RD is characterised by photopsia, floaters and extension of RD up to the ora serrata.' Choose the correct verdict:
opts: True - all three features are present in tractional RD
False - the bracket marks all three as absent (-) in tractional RD
False - only photopsia is absent, floaters and ora serrata extension are present
True - they are present in tractional RD but absent in exudative RD
questions.exp: For tractional RD, photopsia, floaters and extension of RD till ora serrata are grouped by a bracket with (-). (Book p171)

questions.q: Which pair gives the loss of vision and shape of RD in exudative RD?
questions.exp: Exudative RD: loss of vision sudden, painless; shape of RD convex. (Book p171)

questions.q: In a patient with exudative RD, the subretinal fluid moves when the head position is changed. What does the book call this feature?
questions.exp: Exudative RD hallmark features: Shifting fluid (with shifting head position). (Book p171)

questions.q: What is the treatment of secondary (tractional or exudative) RD in the table?
questions.exp: Treatment (spanning both columns): Treat the cause. (Book p171)
